description: Dynamic Sports Plays review, checked 7 Nov 2026: passes from $100 a day to $4,999 a year, a 64% win rate claim with no log, no refunds, and 7 buyer reviews.
dek: A pick service that says it has served 125,000 members since 2013 and wins 64% of its picks. It sells passes from $100 a day to $4,999 a year, all final sale. We found no public record of its picks, and its CapperTek listing shows no documented record at all.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a record for Dynamic Sports Plays, and we found no full, time stamped log of its picks anywhere. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Dynamic Sports Plays is a working website that sells pick passes, with social accounts that post winning tickets. It does not name an owner, a company or an address, and it gives only an email address and a contact form. That is very little to go on for a service charging up to $4,999.

Its record is entirely its own claim. The FAQ says it has kept "a consistent win rate of 64%" since 2013, and the homepage shows parlay tickets such as +7495. We found no pick log behind any of it. Its listing on CapperTek, a marketplace that tracks picks, said it "does not have a documented record yet" and had posted no picks.
Treat Dynamic Sports Plays as an expensive, unproven seller. The terms say every purchase is final, so a buyer who is unhappy after one day has no remedy.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the Dynamic Sports Plays pricing page on 7 Nov 2026 (the Get Picks link opens it). Every plan adds a processing fee at checkout. The terms say all packages are one time, fixed term purchases that do not auto renew, although the page labels three plans "Every week", "Every month" and "Every year".
pricing: No refund. Plan text says "Profit guaranteed", but the footer and terms say no outcome or profit is guaranteed
No refund. Listed plays exclude parlays, unlike the shorter plans
guarantee: There is no guarantee, and the site says so in several places. The FAQ says all purchases are final with no refunds because picks are time sensitive digital products, and the terms say refunds are not provided once access is granted. The terms also say "We do not guarantee outcomes or profits."

One line contradicts that: the Daily All Access Plan description ends with "Profit guaranteed with the best in the business." A buyer should read that as sales copy. Nothing on the site explains what would happen if a day lost, and the refund rules leave no room for a payout. The terms also allow the seller to suspend an account for sharing picks without a refund.

claims_note: A 64% win rate across all sports for 13 years would be extraordinary, and the site offers nothing to check it against. Win rate alone also says little here, because the service rates plays from 5 to 25 units and sells parlays. A few large losing plays can outweigh many small winners, and a parlay ticket at +7495 is one winning slip, not a measure of skill.

The history is hard to pin down. The site says 2013, but the domain dynamicsportsplays.com was registered on 22 Apr 2016, according to the .com registry, and the earliest Wayback Machine capture we found is from Aug 2018. The business could have started elsewhere, such as on social media, but we found no record of that.

Small inconsistencies: the units page lists NFL, college football, NBA, college basketball and MLB, while the FAQ adds the NHL. The terms say users must be 18, while the site footer says 21. The media logos are not linked to any coverage.
record: Independently verifiable: nothing we could find. There is no full, time stamped log of every pick with the line, odds and stake on the site or on a third party tracker. Picks appear on a members only "Your Picks" page and by email, according to the FAQ. On 7 Nov 2026 the Dynamic Sports Plays listing on CapperTek showed no documented record, no picks and no packages for sale, even though customer reviews there quote unit totals.

Seller marketing: the 64% win rate, the membership and country counts, and the winning tickets on the homepage. Reviewers on CapperTek repeat unit totals such as +243.39 units in early 2025, but these appear to be the service's own reported numbers, not separate measurements, and none comes with a log.
We found no court or regulator action involving Dynamic Sports Plays in our searches. With no legal name or owner given, we could not search further.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Dynamic Sports Plays is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: the FAQ claims a 64% win rate since 2013. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: The only buyer reviews we found are seven on CapperTek, all positive, from six usernames, posted between Nov 2023 and Apr 2025. Most reviewers had been with the service for days or weeks, and several quote unit totals that no record we could open supports. We found no reviews on BBB, SiteJabber (which now redirects to SmartCustomer), Reddit or the betting forums.

customers.text: A buyer said he joined in early October 2023, profited over 36 units in his first month and, betting $100 a unit, made over $3,600, so he signed up again. He gave no pick list.

A buyer said he found the service on Instagram, tried two daily packages that went 2-1 and 3-1, then a 3 day package, and claimed an 11-3 run that doubled his bankroll in five days. He cited the service's claim of being in the game since 2013.

One username posted twice. About a week in, he described a 4 leg parlay at +1348 that cashed after the service told members to parlay all its picks; in 2025 he said he had used the service since Dec 2023 and quoted +79.87 units for March and +243.39 units for 2025 so far, praising the WHALE, MEGA MAX and MAX unit tiers.
A reviewer starting his second month said he profited over 27 units the previous month and was up 42 units so far in January, and that "The stats show it all." No stats were linked.

A reviewer about a week in said he had seen a 73% win rate including parlays, with 1 to 4 picks a day, and that the service explained its unit system when he asked. One week is far too short to judge a handicapper.
A reviewer just over a month in said he had doubled his bankroll, cited a 9-0 whale run and an 11-3 March Madness run, and praised fast replies to Instagram messages. He gave no log.

BBB returned no results for the name, and SmartCustomer showed 0 reviews for dynamicsportsplays.com. Trustpilot refused our request, the Instagram profile showed "Profile isn't available" to a logged out visitor, and searches found no Reddit, TheRX, Covers or SBR thread. The TikTok account had 473 followers and 97 videos.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the pages we opened.

The service holds a CapperTek "Verified Service" listing. CapperTek's FAQ says verified means a verification banner and an open line of communication to resolve complaints, not a check of results, and this listing has no tracked picks. The positive reviews on it cannot be compared to any record.
The site markets heavily through winning tickets and social media, which show only the bets the seller chooses to show.
strengths: Prices and processing fees are shown before checkout, and the terms say packages do not auto renew.
The FAQ and units page explain how many picks to expect (1 to 4 a day) and how the 5 to 25 unit scale works.
Several reviewers say support answers quickly by Instagram message.
concerns: No pick log anywhere, and the CapperTek listing has no documented record, so the 64% win rate claim cannot be checked.
No named owner, company or address.
High prices, up to $899 a month and $4,999 a year, with every sale final.
A "Profit guaranteed" line on the daily plan that the site's own terms contradict.
Marketing leans on parlays and winning tickets, and stakes run as high as 25 units.
All customer evidence is from one site, mostly from buyers in their first weeks.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a working website that sells pick passes and has buyer reviews on CapperTek. It names no owner, company or address, and we could not verify its 64% win rate or its membership claims.
How much does Dynamic Sports Plays cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 it charged $100 for a day, $249 for 3 days, $399 for 7 days, $899 for 30 days and $4,999 for a year, each plus a processing fee from $4 to $212.50. All purchases are final with no refunds.
Does Dynamic Sports Plays have a verified record?
No. We found no full log of its picks, its CapperTek listing showed no documented record, and Watchdog has no graded record for it. The 64% figure comes only from its own FAQ.
Is Dynamic Sports Plays worth it?

For the money you get 1 to 4 picks a day across major U.S. sports, rated on a 5 to 25 unit scale, plus parlays on shorter plans. What is unproven is whether those picks win over time, since no record exists to check, and a buyer cannot get money back if they lose.
